verdict.rationale: Logseq's own Publishing feature turns a graph into a single-page web app, and you choose what goes in by marking pages `publish:: true`, since nothing is public by default. Published sites also pick up config.edn and custom CSS/JS. A community user confirms they use the publishing features and self-host their graphs, which suggests you still need outside hosting to put the site online, so it can't be done entirely within the app. Missing for 10: evidence of built-in hosting or deployment without leaving the app, explicit confirmation that page and block links still work on the published site, and fuller hands-on corroboration of the digital-garden experience.
